author: Lance Tormey
title: Would-Be Motorhome Bandit Turns Yakima Garage into Wrecking Ball - NewsBreak
text:
By Lance Tormey ,
13 hours ago
A 38-year-old man is facing a charge of burglary and malicious mischief after police say he tried to steal a motorhome in Yakima on Saturday.
POLICE SAY THE SUSPECT WAS FOUND RAMMING THE GARAGE DOORS Yakima Police say while trying to steal the motorhome the suspect caused more than $20,000 in damage. Officers were called to a home in the 1900 block of South 44th Avenue at about 3:30 am Saturday after the homeowners heard ‚Äúloud banging sounds‚Äù coming from an detached garage on the property. They found the 38-year-old suspect behind the wheel repeatedly ramming the garage doors attempting to flee in the stolen motorhome.
READ MORE: VOTE FOR YAKIMA BEST BEER CITY
THE SUSPECT WAS ARRESTED WITHOUT ANY PROBLEMS According to an affidavit from the Yakima County Prosecutors Office when Officers arrived they ordered the suspect to come out of the motorhome where he was quickly arrested.¬†Police say the suspect wasn‚Äôt successful in stealing the motorhome but he did severely damage the motorhome, the detached garage as well as a small boat and trailer that were also in the garage. Damage is estimated at more than $20,000.¬†Police say the damage was bad enough that the garage has the potential to collapse.
YPD/Lance Tormey THE SUSPECT IS BEING HELD IN THE YAKIMA COUNTY JAIL The 38-year-old suspect was arrested on Second Degree Burglary, First Degree Malicious Mischief, Attempted Theft of a Motor Vehicle and First Degree Vehicle Prowl. He was booked into the Yakima County jail. It‚Äôs not known how the suspect was able to start the motorhome or how he gained access to the garage. The investigation into the crime continues today.

Canva Health Care Washington Ranked #10 compared to the rest of the country with our Health Care. This encompassed citizen's access, quality, and outcomes. Canva Natural Environment Washington Ranked #11 compared to the rest of the country for our Natural Environment. This makes total sense; we get all four seasons (sometimes in the same week) and are¬†surrounded by natural beauty. In the ranking methodology , they looked at pollution threats vs combating those threats as well as the quality of the air and water in our state. Canva Education Washington Ranked #13 compared to the rest of the country in regards to Education. In this ranking it look at metrics linked to pre-school all the way through high school and higher education. Canva Fiscal Stability Washington Ranked #14 compared to the rest of the U.S. in our Fiscal Stability. What does that mean? In a nutshell, it is how well our state government is doing with its projects and the effects on our residents. Canva Economy Washington Ranked #14 in the U.S. in our economy. This ranking looked at the labor market, economic growth, as well as Washington‚Äôs business environment.
Canva Opportunity This where Washington has quite a bit of room to improve, our residents Opportunity ranked at #37 compared to the rest of the country. This ranking looked closer at equality, affordability as well as economic opportunity in each state.
Canva Crime & Corrections Another area that Washington has room to improve upon is Crime and Corrections, where we ranked #39 in the United States. Even though (according to USNews.com ) crime in America has declined over time, more and more people are imprisoned (more than in other developed countries). The more people in jail, the more of a burden it is on our state and the taxpayers. Canva Washington's Over All Ranking!
